output.summary: SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with a significantly increased risk of ischemic stroke, both during acute infection and for up to 12 months afterward. Proposed mechanisms include endotheliopathy, platelet dysfunction, and a hypercoagulable/thromboinflammatory state. Patients with pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors including atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and diabetes appear to be at compounded risk. COVID-19-associated coagulopathy may act as an additional precipitant to pre-existing thromboembolic risk factors.

key_clinical_evidence: Acute ischemic stroke is a clinical syndrome plus neuroimaging diagnosis; CT first excludes hemorrhage and unmasks the tPA decision
Time of last known well governs IV thrombolysis eligibility (≤4.5h standard; selected up to 9h with imaging mismatch per WAKE-UP/EXTEND)
proximal vascular occlusion on CTA opens the mechanical thrombectomy pathway up to 24h per DAWN/DEFUSE-3 selection criteria
TOAST classification by mechanism (large-artery, cardioembolic, small-vessel, other, undetermined) drives secondary prevention strategy
Normal sinus rhythm on initial ECG does NOT exclude paroxysmal AF — extended cardiac monitoring is required, especially in cryptogenic stroke
AF off anticoagulation is a high-risk cardioembolic stroke mechanism with high recurrence risk
DOACs have superior safety-efficacy profile to warfarin for non-valvular AF
Post-COVID AF and inflammation may increase short-term thromboembolic risk
Off-pathway modality for order_advanced_imaging (modality=amyloid_PET): Amyloid PET has no role in acute ischemic stroke evaluation and incurs substantial cost without altering management
Off-pathway modality for order_advanced_imaging (modality=DaTscan): Dopamine transporter SPECT is indicated for parkinsonian syndromes, not vascular stroke workup
Off-pathway modality for order_advanced_imaging (modality=FDG_PET): FDG-PET (neurodegenerative/oncologic indications) has no role in routine ischemic stroke workup
Tier per the July 2026 clinical review: Non-contrast CT is the required first-line study in the acute window; MRI adds tissue-based selection and is not mandatory for the diagnosis.

AHA/ASA 2026 sequencing: glucose is checked before thrombolysis, but routine CBC/coagulation results are not awaited without a reason to expect abnormality; ECG/troponin do not delay reperfusion, and CTA/CTP do not wait for creatinine.

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Elena Vasquez is a 68-year-old right-handed woman with a history of atrial fibrillation (previously on warfarin, self-discontinued 6 months ago), hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and recent COVID-19 infection approximately 8 weeks ago, who was brought to the emergency department by her daughter after acute onset of right-sided weakness and speech difficulty. The daughter reports that she spoke with her mother on the phone at 09:00 this morning and she sounded entirely normal. When the daughter arrived at her mother's apartment at 11:15 for a planned lunch, she found her sitting on the kitchen floor, leaning against the cabinets. The patient was attempting to speak but producing only fragmented words. Her right arm was limp at her side and she was unable to stand. There was a broken plate on the floor suggesting she had dropped it. The daughter called 911 immediately. EMS arrived at 11:28 and documented right facial droop, right hemiparesis, and expressive aphasia. A prehospital stroke alert was activated. Field glucose was 142 mg/dL. The patient was transported emergently to this comprehensive stroke center, arriving at 11:52. On the cardiac monitor, she was noted to be in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. The patient appeared frightened and was producing short phrases with significant word-finding difficulty but could nod appropriately to simple yes-or-no questions. There was no reported preceding headache, seizure activity, recent head trauma, or fever. The daughter confirms that her mother had COVID-19 approximately 8 weeks ago with cough and fatigue lasting about 10 days, managed entirely at home without hospitalization. She had not been vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2. The daughter also confirms her mother stopped taking warfarin about 6 months ago because of bleeding gums and had not followed up with her cardiologist since. Last known well time is established at 09:00, approximately 2 hours and 52 minutes prior to ED arrival.
